question: Europe’s manufacturing sector producing metal accessories and components for use in fashion, leather goods, footwear and luxury items is a highly specialised industry that brings high added value through processes such as die-forging, precision casting, precision machining, assembly and galvanic treatments.

Article 60(2) of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 determines the origin of goods on the basis of where they underwent their last, substantial, economically justified processing or working. Meanwhile, Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 has brought in the digital product passport (DPP) with a view to improving value chain traceability.
In light of the delegated acts drawn up in relation to the DPP and the need to safeguard the competitiveness of European manufacturing: 1.

Does the Commission intend to include information on customs origin and the main processing phases in the DPP, and set specific traceability requirements for metal accessories used in the fashion industry?
Will it examine whether the current non-preferential origin rules are appropriate and increase the interoperability between the DPP and customs information?
